He said: Yes, I have done what is right, and the experienced and wise will confirm it. Whoever follows him will be guided to all right conduct, and whoever disbelieves in him will be recompensed with disbelief. When they drank treachery and disbelief, they found themselves averse to the truth. I see God the Prophet with an honest opinion and God is the judge who does not act unjustly So he supported him and gave him authority over them, and he was their best supporter. Ka'b was left dead among them, and after his death, the Nadir tribe was humiliated. On the palms of our hands, then we have exposed his masculinity with our hands By the command of Muhammad, he sent Ka'b's brother a secret message to Ka'b at night. What he disliked, he brought it down with cunning, and Mahmoud is a trustworthy and courageous brother. Those are the Banu Nadir in a house of evil. They were destroyed for what they had committed. The next day, they attacked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he was watching them. Ghassan Al-Hama supported him against the enemies and he was their minister. He said peace and they ruled, but they turned away and disobeyed their order, lying and forgery. They tasted the consequences of their deed, and every three of them would receive a camel. They deliberately moved to Qainuqa and Ghodar, from which there were palm trees and houses. He said: Among the poems said about Banu Nadir was the saying of Ibn al-Qayyim al-Absi, and it is said that Qais bin Bahr bin Tarif said it. Ibn Hisham al-Ashja’i said: My family is a sacrifice for a man who will not perish. The Jews were expelled by Al-Hassan Al-Maznam. They take a nap in the embers of the tamarisk tree, and they exchanged the soft wood for the muzzled wood. If my opinion of Muhammad is true, they will see his horses between the two mountains and he will be seen gliding. Amr ibn Bahtha leads the prayer. They are enemies, and no one is as friendly as a criminal. They are heroes, daring in the battlefield, shaking the edges of the straightened rope. And every thin blade is an inherited sword from the time of Ad and Jurhum. Who will convey my message to the Quraysh? Is there anyone more honorable than them? Know that your brother, Muhammad, is born and bred between Al-Hujun and Zamzam. So, obey Him in truth, and your affairs will be settled, and you will rise from this world to the highest level. A prophet whom God has bestowed upon you mercy. Do not ask him about an unseen matter. Indeed, in Badr, by my life, there was a lesson for you, O Quraysh, and a heart that was gathered. The next day he came to Khazraj, intending to come to you, obedient to the Great and Generous One. Together with the Holy Spirit, he defeats his enemy, a true Messenger from the Most Gracious, with a teacher. A Messenger from the Most Gracious reciting His Book. When the truth was illuminated, he did not falter. I see his command increasing in every place in elevation for the command of God Almighty Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, has included here many poems containing morals, sermons, wisdom, and details of the story. We have left out the rest for the sake of brevity and contentment with what we have mentioned, and praise and thanks be to God. Ibn Ishaq said: The Battle of Banu Nadir took place after the Battle of Uhud and after the Battle of Bir Ma'unah. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah that he said: The Battle of Banu Nadir took place six months after the Battle of Badr.
59:4: God Almighty tells us that everything in the heavens and on the earth glorifies Him, sanctifies Him, prays to Him, and declares His Oneness, as He says: “The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is therein glorify Him. There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification.” And He says: And He is the Exalted in Might, meaning the Invincible, the Wise in His power and His law. And He says: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, meaning the Jews of Banu Nadir. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Zuhri and others said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, he made a truce with them and gave them a covenant and protection on the condition that he would not fight them and they would not fight him. They broke the covenant that was between them and him, so God brought down upon them His unstoppable wrath and sent down upon them His unstoppable judgment. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) expelled them and drove them out of their strong fortresses, which the Muslims had not coveted and which they had thought would protect them from God’s wrath. But it did not avail them anything against God, and what they had not expected came to them from God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent them and expelled them from Medina. Some of them went to Adhra’at in the upper reaches of Syria, which is the land of gathering and resurrection. Some of them went to Khaybar, and he had settled them there on the condition that they would have whatever their camels carried. They destroyed the movable property in their homes that could not be carried with them. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, you people of knowledge.” Al-Absar means think about the consequences of those who disobey God's command, disobey His Messenger, and deny His Book. How will His humiliating punishment befall them in this world, along with the painful torment He has in store for them in the Hereafter? Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Dawud Sufyan told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka`b ibn Malik, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the infidels of Quraysh wrote to Ibn Ubayy and those who were with him who worshipped idols from the Aws and Khazraj, while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Medina at that time before the Battle of Badr: You have given refuge to our companion, and we swear by God that we will fight him or expel you or we will march against you all together until we kill your fighters and take your women captive. When this reached Abdullah ibn Ubayy and those who were with him from the idol worshippers, they gathered to fight the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When this reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he met them and said: “The threat of Quraysh from you has reached the limits. They plotted against you more than you want to plot against yourselves. They want to fight your sons and brothers.” When they heard that from the Prophet, they dispersed. This reached the infidels of Quraysh, so after the Battle of Badr, the infidels of Quraysh wrote to the Jews: You are the people of the circle and the fortresses. You will either fight with our companion or we will do such and such, and nothing will stand between us and your women’s servants, which are the anklets. When their letter reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Banu Nadir were certain of the treachery, so they sent to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Come out to us with thirty men from your companions, and let thirty rabbis come out from us until we meet at the middle place, and let them listen to you. If they believe you and have faith in you, we will believe in you. The next day, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them with his troops and besieged them, saying to them: By God, you will not believe in me except through a covenant that you make with me. They refused to give him a covenant, so he fought them that day. Then the next day he went to Banu Qurayzah with his troops, leaving Banu Nadir and calling them to make a covenant with him. They made a covenant with him, so he turned away from them and went to Banu Nadir with his troops. He fought them until they agreed to leave. Banu Nadir fled and carried what the camels could carry of their belongings, the doors of their houses and their wood. The date palms of Banu Nadir were specifically for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God gave them to him and singled them out for him, as God Almighty said: And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger from them, you did not urge upon it any horses or camels, meaning without fighting. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave most of it to the Muhajireen, dividing it among them and dividing it to two men from the Ansar, who were in need. He did not divide it from the Ansar except them. The rest of it was the charity of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Which is in the hands of the Banu Fatima, and let us mention the summary of the Battle of Banu Nadir in brief, and God is the helper. The reason for this, as mentioned by the authors of the campaigns and biographies, was that when the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were killed at Bir Ma’unah, and they were seventy, and Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri escaped from them, then while he was on his way back to Medina, he killed two men from Banu Amir, and they had a covenant from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a guarantee of safety that Amr did not know about. So when he returned, he informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have killed two men for whose blood money I owe them. There was a covenant and agreement between Banu al-Nadir and Banu Amir, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Banu al-Nadir to ask for their help in the blood money of those two men, and the homes of Banu al-Nadir were outside Medina, miles to the east of it. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in his book, Al-Seerah: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Banu Nadir to ask for their help in the blood money of those two men killed from Banu Amir, who were killed by Amr bin Umayya Al-Damri for the protection that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made for them, according to what Yazid bin Ruman told me. There was a covenant and an oath between Banu Nadir and Banu Amir. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them to ask for their help in the blood money of those two men, they said: Yes, O Abu Al-Qasim, we will help you in whatever you like of what you asked us for. Then some of them met in private and said: You will not find a man in such a state as this - and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, was next to a wall of one of their houses - so who is the man who will climb up to this house and throw a rock at him and relieve us of him? Amr ibn Jahsh ibn Ka’b appointed one of them for this purpose, and he said, I will do it. So he went up to throw a rock at him, as he had said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with a group of his companions, among them Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali, may God be pleased with them. Then the report of what the people wanted came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the sky, so he stood up and went back to Medina. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had delayed his companions, they went in search of him and found a man coming from Medina. They asked him about him and he said, I saw him entering Medina. So the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came until they reached him. He told them the report of what the Jews had intended to do to him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to prepare for war and to march against them. Then he marched until he came down to them and they took refuge in the fortresses. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the palm trees to be cut down and burned. They called out to him, O Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption on earth and criticize those who did it, so what about cutting down and burning the palm trees? A group of Banu Auf ibn al-Khazraj, including Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Wadi’ah, Malik ibn Abi Qawqal, Suwayd and Da’is, had sent word to Banu al-Nadir that they should remain steadfast and resist, for we will not surrender to you. If you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you leave, we will leave with you. They waited for that to help them, but they did not do so, so God cast terror into their hearts. They asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to expel them and refrain from shedding their blood on the condition that they would have whatever money the camels carried of their wealth except the ring. He did so, and they carried as much of their wealth as the camels could carry. A man among them would demolish his house to the exclusion of its door and place it on the back of his camel and set off with it. They went out to Khaybar, and some of them went to Syria and left the wealth for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to place it wherever he wished. He divided it among the first emigrants without the Ansar, except for Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujana - Samak ibn Kharshah. They mentioned poverty, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them something. He said: No one from Banu Nadir converted to Islam except two men: Yamin ibn Amr ibn Ka’b, the uncle of Amr ibn Jahash, and Abu Sa’d ibn Wahb. They converted to Islam with their wealth and preserved it. Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the family of Yamin told me that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Yamin: Have you not seen what I have suffered from your cousin and what they intend to do to me? So Yamin ibn Amr made a promise to a man to kill Amr ibn Jahash, so he killed him, as they claim. Ibn Ishaq said: The entire Surah Al-Hashr was revealed regarding Banu Nadir. Yunus ibn Bakir narrated this from Ibn Ishaq in a similar manner. God the Almighty said: It is He who brought forth those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture meaning Banu Nadir from their homes at the first gathering. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Sa’d, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever doubts that the land of gathering is here, meaning Syria, should read this verse: It is He who brought forth those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Go forth. They said: To where? He said: To the place of assembly. Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled Banu Al-Nadir, he said: This is the first of the assembly, and I am following in its footsteps. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Uday, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, with the same chain of transmission. And the Almighty’s saying: You did not think that they would come out meaning during the period of your siege of them, which was short and was six days despite the strength and fortification of their fortresses. For this reason, the Almighty said: And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came to them from where they had not expected. That is, what came to them from God’s command came to them from where they had not expected, as the Almighty said in the other verse: “Those before them had already plotted, but God attacked their structure from the foundations, so the roof collapsed upon them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.” God the Almighty says: {And He cast terror into their hearts} meaning fear, panic and alarm. How could that not happen to them when the One who was victorious through terror besieged them for a month’s journey, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And His statement: {They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers}, Ibn Ishaq’s explanation of that has already been given above, which is the demolition of what they considered good of their roofs and doors and loading them on camels. This is what Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others said. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, would fight them, and if he gained control of a path or a house, he would demolish its walls to make room for the fighting. And if the Jews gained control of a place or overcame a path or a house, they would dig from the backs of it, then fortify and defend it. God the Almighty says: {So take admonition, you who have vision}. And his statement: And had it not been that God decreed exile upon them, He would have punished them in this world. That is, had it not been that God decreed this exile upon them, which is exile from their homes and wealth, they would have had another punishment from God, such as killing, captivity, and the like. Al-Zuhri said this on the authority of Urwah, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd, because God had decreed upon them that He would punish them in this world, along with what He had prepared for them in the Hereafter of punishment in the fire of Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Saleh, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me: Then there was the battle of Banu Al-Nadir, and they were a group of Jews, six months after the Battle of Badr. Their camp was in a district of Madinah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them until they agreed to exile, and they were to have whatever money and goods the camels carried except for the ring, which is the weapon. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, exiled them towards Syria. He said: And exile was written for them in verses of the Torah, and they were from a tribe that had not been exiled before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was empowered over them, and God revealed about them: “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think that they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God. But God came to them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, O you of knowledge.” The eyes * And had it not been that God had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire. * That is because they opposed God and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God - then indeed, God is severe in penalty. * Whether you cut down a palm grove or leave it standing on its roots, it was by God’s permission, and [He does so] in order to disgrace the wicked. And Ikrimah said: Exile means killing, and in another narration from him: annihilation. Qatada said: Exile means people leaving one country for another. Ad-Dahhak said: He expelled them to Syria and gave every three a camel and a water skin, so this is the exiling. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Ahmad bin Kamil Al-Qadi told us, Muhammad bin Saeed Al-Awfi told us, my father told us, on the authority of my uncle, my father told us, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had besieged them until he had exhausted them, so they gave him whatever he wanted from them, so he made peace with them on the condition that he spared their bloodshed, expel them from their land, homes and homelands, and send them to Adhraat Al-Sham, giving each three of them a camel and a water skin, and that he would expel them from their land to another land. It was also narrated from the hadith of Yaqub bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Ja’far, on the authority of Mahmud bin Muhammad bin Maslama, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Muhammad bin Maslama, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him to Banu Al-Nadir and ordered him to give them three days’ respite in the expulsion. God the Almighty says: {And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire} meaning it is inevitable and inevitable for them. God the Almighty says: {That is because they opposed God and His Messenger} meaning that God did that to them and gave power over them to His Messenger and His believing servants, because they opposed God and His Messenger and denied what God revealed to His previous messengers in the good tidings of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and they knew that as they knew their own sons. Then He said: {And whoever opposes God - then indeed, God is severe in penalty}. God the Almighty says: {Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by permission of God, and in order that He might disgrace the wicked} Layyin is a type of date, and it is good. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the date that differs from Ajwa and Barni. Many of the commentators said: Layyin is the variety of dates other than Ajwa. Ibn Jarir said: It refers to all date palms. He narrated it from Mujahid and it also refers to Al-Buwayrah. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) besieged them, he ordered their date palms to be cut down as a humiliation, terror, and intimidation to their hearts. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: Banu Nadir sent word to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): You forbid corruption, so why do you order the cutting down of trees? Then God revealed this noble verse: Whatever palm trees you cut down and whatever trees you left, all of it was by His permission, will, decree, and pleasure. In it is a slap to the enemy, a disgrace to them, and a humiliation to their noses. Mujahid said: Some of the Muhajireen forbade others from cutting down palm trees, and they said: They are only spoils of war for the Muslims. So the Qur’an was revealed confirming those who forbade cutting them down and absolving those who cut them down from sin. They only cut them down and left them with His permission. Something similar to this was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Nasa’i said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Affan, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi ‘Umrah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, regarding the verse: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by permission of God, and in order to disgrace the wicked. He said: They were to force them to leave their fortresses and they were ordered to cut down the palm trees, so this caused confusion in their hearts. The Muslims said: We cut down some and left others, so let us ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Do we have a reward for what we cut down? And do we bear a sin for what we left? Then God revealed, Whatever palm trees you cut down, and Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Sufyan ibn Waki’ told us, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Jabir, and on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: He gave them permission to cut down palm trees, but then made things difficult for them. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, O Messenger of God, there is a sin upon us for what we cut down, or a burden upon us for what we left behind. Then God, the Almighty, revealed, Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by God’s permission. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut down the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir and burned them. The two authors of the Sahih included it in a similar narration from Musa ibn Uqbah, and the wording of al-Bukhari from the path of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I fought al-Nadir and Qurayza, so he expelled Banu al-Nadir and left Qurayza alone and was merciful to them until he fought Qurayza, so he killed some of their men and took them captive and divided their women, children and wealth among the Muslims except for some of them who joined the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he granted them security and they converted to Islam, and he expelled all the Jews of Madinah, Banu Qaynuqa’, who were the people of Abdullah ibn Salam, and the Jews of Banu Haritha and all the Jews of Madinah. They also have it from Qutaybah, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burned the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir and cut them down, and they were al-Buwayrah, so God, the Almighty, revealed about it: Whatever you cut down of palm trees or… You left it standing on its foundations, so by God’s permission, and to disgrace the wicked.” Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, narrated on the authority of Juwayriyah bint Asma’, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burned the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir, and Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said about it: The fire in Bouira was so widespread that it was easy for the leaders of Bani Luay Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith replied: May God perpetuate this act and burn its regions with fire. You will know which of us is pure and which of us is pure And thus it was narrated by Al-Bukhari, but Ibn Ishaq did not mention it. Muhammad Ibn Ishaq said, and Ka`b Ibn Malik said, mentioning the expulsion of Banu Nadir and the killing of Ibn Al-Ashraf: I was disgraced by her treachery, joy, just like time, with its changing and revolving ways. This is because they disbelieved in a great Lord whose command is a great command. They were both given understanding and knowledge, and a warner came to them from God. A true warner who delivered clear books and verses that enlighten. They said: You have not brought anything true, and you are worthy of our denial. He said: Yes, I have done what is right, and the experienced and wise will confirm it. Whoever follows him will be guided to all right conduct, and whoever disbelieves in him will be recompensed with disbelief. When they drank treachery and disbelief, they found themselves averse to the truth. I see God the Prophet with an honest opinion and God is the judge who does not act unjustly So he supported him and gave him authority over them, and he was their best supporter. Ka'b was left dead among them, and after his death, the Nadir tribe was humiliated. On the palms of our hands, then we have exposed his masculinity with our hands By the command of Muhammad, he sent Ka'b's brother a secret message to Ka'b at night. What he disliked, he brought it down with cunning, and Mahmoud is a trustworthy and courageous brother. Those are the Banu Nadir in a house of evil. They were destroyed for what they had committed. The next day, they attacked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he was watching them. Ghassan Al-Hama supported him against the enemies and he was their minister. He said peace and they ruled, but they turned away and disobeyed their order, lying and forgery. They tasted the consequences of their deed, and every three of them would receive a camel. They deliberately moved to Qainuqa and Ghodar, from which there were palm trees and houses. He said: Among the poems said about Banu Nadir was the saying of Ibn al-Qayyim al-Absi, and it is said that Qais bin Bahr bin Tarif said it. Ibn Hisham al-Ashja’i said: My family is a sacrifice for a man who will not perish. The Jews were expelled by Al-Hassan Al-Maznam. They take a nap in the embers of the tamarisk tree, and they exchanged the soft wood for the muzzled wood. If my opinion of Muhammad is true, they will see his horses between the two mountains and he will be seen gliding. Amr ibn Bahtha leads the prayer. They are enemies, and no one is as friendly as a criminal. They are heroes, daring in the battlefield, shaking the edges of the straightened rope. And every thin blade is an inherited sword from the time of Ad and Jurhum. Who will convey my message to the Quraysh? Is there anyone more honorable than them? Know that your brother, Muhammad, is born and bred between Al-Hujun and Zamzam. So, obey Him in truth, and your affairs will be settled, and you will rise from this world to the highest level. A prophet whom God has bestowed upon you mercy. Do not ask him about an unseen matter. Indeed, in Badr, by my life, there was a lesson for you, O Quraysh, and a heart that was gathered. The next day he came to Khazraj, intending to come to you, obedient to the Great and Generous One. Together with the Holy Spirit, he defeats his enemy, a true Messenger from the Most Gracious, with a teacher. A Messenger from the Most Gracious reciting His Book. When the truth was illuminated, he did not falter. I see his command increasing in every place in elevation for the command of God Almighty Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, has included here many poems containing morals, sermons, wisdom, and details of the story. We have left out the rest for the sake of brevity and contentment with what we have mentioned, and praise and thanks be to God. Ibn Ishaq said: The Battle of Banu Nadir took place after the Battle of Uhud and after the Battle of Bir Ma'unah. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah that he said: The Battle of Banu Nadir took place six months after the Battle of Badr.
59:5: God Almighty tells us that everything in the heavens and on the earth glorifies Him, sanctifies Him, prays to Him, and declares His Oneness, as He says: “The seven heavens and the earth and whatever is therein glorify Him. There is not a thing but glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification.” And He says: And He is the Exalted in Might, meaning the Invincible, the Wise in His power and His law. And He says: It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture, meaning the Jews of Banu Nadir. Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Al-Zuhri and others said: When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to Medina, he made a truce with them and gave them a covenant and protection on the condition that he would not fight them and they would not fight him. They broke the covenant that was between them and him, so God brought down upon them His unstoppable wrath and sent down upon them His unstoppable judgment. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) expelled them and drove them out of their strong fortresses, which the Muslims had not coveted and which they had thought would protect them from God’s wrath. But it did not avail them anything against God, and what they had not expected came to them from God. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent them and expelled them from Medina. Some of them went to Adhra’at in the upper reaches of Syria, which is the land of gathering and resurrection. Some of them went to Khaybar, and he had settled them there on the condition that they would have whatever their camels carried. They destroyed the movable property in their homes that could not be carried with them. For this reason, God the Almighty said: “They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, you people of knowledge.” Al-Absar means think about the consequences of those who disobey God's command, disobey His Messenger, and deny His Book. How will His humiliating punishment befall them in this world, along with the painful torment He has in store for them in the Hereafter? Abu Dawud said: Muhammad ibn Dawud Sufyan told us, Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Ka`b ibn Malik, on the authority of a man from the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, that the infidels of Quraysh wrote to Ibn Ubayy and those who were with him who worshipped idols from the Aws and Khazraj, while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was in Medina at that time before the Battle of Badr: You have given refuge to our companion, and we swear by God that we will fight him or expel you or we will march against you all together until we kill your fighters and take your women captive. When this reached Abdullah ibn Ubayy and those who were with him from the idol worshippers, they gathered to fight the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace. When this reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, he met them and said: “The threat of Quraysh from you has reached the limits. They plotted against you more than you want to plot against yourselves. They want to fight your sons and brothers.” When they heard that from the Prophet, they dispersed. This reached the infidels of Quraysh, so after the Battle of Badr, the infidels of Quraysh wrote to the Jews: You are the people of the circle and the fortresses. You will either fight with our companion or we will do such and such, and nothing will stand between us and your women’s servants, which are the anklets. When their letter reached the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, Banu Nadir were certain of the treachery, so they sent to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Come out to us with thirty men from your companions, and let thirty rabbis come out from us until we meet at the middle place, and let them listen to you. If they believe you and have faith in you, we will believe in you. The next day, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them with his troops and besieged them, saying to them: By God, you will not believe in me except through a covenant that you make with me. They refused to give him a covenant, so he fought them that day. Then the next day he went to Banu Qurayzah with his troops, leaving Banu Nadir and calling them to make a covenant with him. They made a covenant with him, so he turned away from them and went to Banu Nadir with his troops. He fought them until they agreed to leave. Banu Nadir fled and carried what the camels could carry of their belongings, the doors of their houses and their wood. The date palms of Banu Nadir were specifically for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. God gave them to him and singled them out for him, as God Almighty said: And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger from them, you did not urge upon it any horses or camels, meaning without fighting. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave most of it to the Muhajireen, dividing it among them and dividing it to two men from the Ansar, who were in need. He did not divide it from the Ansar except them. The rest of it was the charity of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. Which is in the hands of the Banu Fatima, and let us mention the summary of the Battle of Banu Nadir in brief, and God is the helper. The reason for this, as mentioned by the authors of the campaigns and biographies, was that when the companions of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, were killed at Bir Ma’unah, and they were seventy, and Amr ibn Umayyah ad-Damri escaped from them, then while he was on his way back to Medina, he killed two men from Banu Amir, and they had a covenant from the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and a guarantee of safety that Amr did not know about. So when he returned, he informed the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have killed two men for whose blood money I owe them. There was a covenant and agreement between Banu al-Nadir and Banu Amir, so the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Banu al-Nadir to ask for their help in the blood money of those two men, and the homes of Banu al-Nadir were outside Medina, miles to the east of it. Muhammad bin Ishaq bin Yasar said in his book, Al-Seerah: Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, went out to Banu Nadir to ask for their help in the blood money of those two men killed from Banu Amir, who were killed by Amr bin Umayya Al-Damri for the protection that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had made for them, according to what Yazid bin Ruman told me. There was a covenant and an oath between Banu Nadir and Banu Amir. When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, came to them to ask for their help in the blood money of those two men, they said: Yes, O Abu Al-Qasim, we will help you in whatever you like of what you asked us for. Then some of them met in private and said: You will not find a man in such a state as this - and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family and grant them peace, was next to a wall of one of their houses - so who is the man who will climb up to this house and throw a rock at him and relieve us of him? Amr ibn Jahsh ibn Ka’b appointed one of them for this purpose, and he said, I will do it. So he went up to throw a rock at him, as he had said, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was with a group of his companions, among them Abu Bakr, Umar, and Ali, may God be pleased with them. Then the report of what the people wanted came to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, from the sky, so he stood up and went back to Medina. When the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) had delayed his companions, they went in search of him and found a man coming from Medina. They asked him about him and he said, I saw him entering Medina. So the companions of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came until they reached him. He told them the report of what the Jews had intended to do to him, and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered them to prepare for war and to march against them. Then he marched until he came down to them and they took refuge in the fortresses. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) ordered the palm trees to be cut down and burned. They called out to him, O Muhammad, you used to forbid corruption on earth and criticize those who did it, so what about cutting down and burning the palm trees? A group of Banu Auf ibn al-Khazraj, including Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Wadi’ah, Malik ibn Abi Qawqal, Suwayd and Da’is, had sent word to Banu al-Nadir that they should remain steadfast and resist, for we will not surrender to you. If you are fought, we will fight with you, and if you leave, we will leave with you. They waited for that to help them, but they did not do so, so God cast terror into their hearts. They asked the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to expel them and refrain from shedding their blood on the condition that they would have whatever money the camels carried of their wealth except the ring. He did so, and they carried as much of their wealth as the camels could carry. A man among them would demolish his house to the exclusion of its door and place it on the back of his camel and set off with it. They went out to Khaybar, and some of them went to Syria and left the wealth for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace. It was exclusively for the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, to place it wherever he wished. He divided it among the first emigrants without the Ansar, except for Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujana - Samak ibn Kharshah. They mentioned poverty, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them something. He said: No one from Banu Nadir converted to Islam except two men: Yamin ibn Amr ibn Ka’b, the uncle of Amr ibn Jahash, and Abu Sa’d ibn Wahb. They converted to Islam with their wealth and preserved it. Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the family of Yamin told me that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to Yamin: Have you not seen what I have suffered from your cousin and what they intend to do to me? So Yamin ibn Amr made a promise to a man to kill Amr ibn Jahash, so he killed him, as they claim. Ibn Ishaq said: The entire Surah Al-Hashr was revealed regarding Banu Nadir. Yunus ibn Bakir narrated this from Ibn Ishaq in a similar manner. God the Almighty said: It is He who brought forth those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture meaning Banu Nadir from their homes at the first gathering. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Ibn Abi Umar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Abu Sa’d, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Whoever doubts that the land of gathering is here, meaning Syria, should read this verse: It is He who brought forth those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to them: Go forth. They said: To where? He said: To the place of assembly. Abu Saeed Al-Ashja told us, Abu Usama told us, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, expelled Banu Al-Nadir, he said: This is the first of the assembly, and I am following in its footsteps. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Bandar, on the authority of Ibn Abi Uday, on the authority of Aouf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, with the same chain of transmission. And the Almighty’s saying: You did not think that they would come out meaning during the period of your siege of them, which was short and was six days despite the strength and fortification of their fortresses. For this reason, the Almighty said: And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God, but God came to them from where they had not expected. That is, what came to them from God’s command came to them from where they had not expected, as the Almighty said in the other verse: “Those before them had already plotted, but God attacked their structure from the foundations, so the roof collapsed upon them from above them, and the punishment came to them from where they did not perceive.” God the Almighty says: {And He cast terror into their hearts} meaning fear, panic and alarm. How could that not happen to them when the One who was victorious through terror besieged them for a month’s journey, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him. And His statement: {They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers}, Ibn Ishaq’s explanation of that has already been given above, which is the demolition of what they considered good of their roofs and doors and loading them on camels. This is what Urwah ibn Az-Zubayr, Abdur-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and others said. Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: The Messenger of God, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, would fight them, and if he gained control of a path or a house, he would demolish its walls to make room for the fighting. And if the Jews gained control of a place or overcame a path or a house, they would dig from the backs of it, then fortify and defend it. God the Almighty says: {So take admonition, you who have vision}. And his statement: And had it not been that God decreed exile upon them, He would have punished them in this world. That is, had it not been that God decreed this exile upon them, which is exile from their homes and wealth, they would have had another punishment from God, such as killing, captivity, and the like. Al-Zuhri said this on the authority of Urwah, Al-Suddi, and Ibn Zayd, because God had decreed upon them that He would punish them in this world, along with what He had prepared for them in the Hereafter of punishment in the fire of Hell. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdullah bin Saleh, the scribe of Al-Layth, told us, Al-Layth told me, on the authority of Aqeel, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, who said: Urwah bin Al-Zubayr told me: Then there was the battle of Banu Al-Nadir, and they were a group of Jews, six months after the Battle of Badr. Their camp was in a district of Madinah, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, besieged them until they agreed to exile, and they were to have whatever money and goods the camels carried except for the ring, which is the weapon. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, exiled them towards Syria. He said: And exile was written for them in verses of the Torah, and they were from a tribe that had not been exiled before the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was empowered over them, and God revealed about them: “Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth exalts God, and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise. It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think that they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God. But God came to them from where they did not expect and cast terror into their hearts. They destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take heed, O you of knowledge.” The eyes * And had it not been that God had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world, and in the Hereafter they will have the punishment of the Fire. * That is because they opposed God and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God - then indeed, God is severe in penalty. * Whether you cut down a palm grove or leave it standing on its roots, it was by God’s permission, and [He does so] in order to disgrace the wicked. And Ikrimah said: Exile means killing, and in another narration from him: annihilation. Qatada said: Exile means people leaving one country for another. Ad-Dahhak said: He expelled them to Syria and gave every three a camel and a water skin, so this is the exiling. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bayhaqi said: Abu Abdullah Al-Hafiz told us, Ahmad bin Kamil Al-Qadi told us, Muhammad bin Saeed Al-Awfi told us, my father told us, on the authority of my uncle, my father told us, on the authority of my grandfather, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, had besieged them until he had exhausted them, so they gave him whatever he wanted from them, so he made peace with them on the condition that he spared their bloodshed, expel them from their land, homes and homelands, and send them to Adhraat Al-Sham, giving each three of them a camel and a water skin, and that he would expel them from their land to another land. It was also narrated from the hadith of Yaqub bin Muhammad Al-Zuhri, on the authority of Ibrahim bin Ja’far, on the authority of Mahmud bin Muhammad bin Maslama, on the authority of his father, on the authority of his grandfather, on the authority of Muhammad bin Maslama, that the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, sent him to Banu Al-Nadir and ordered him to give them three days’ respite in the expulsion. God the Almighty says: {And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire} meaning it is inevitable and inevitable for them. God the Almighty says: {That is because they opposed God and His Messenger} meaning that God did that to them and gave power over them to His Messenger and His believing servants, because they opposed God and His Messenger and denied what God revealed to His previous messengers in the good tidings of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, and they knew that as they knew their own sons. Then He said: {And whoever opposes God - then indeed, God is severe in penalty}. God the Almighty says: {Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by permission of God, and in order that He might disgrace the wicked} Layyin is a type of date, and it is good. Abu Ubaidah said: It is the date that differs from Ajwa and Barni. Many of the commentators said: Layyin is the variety of dates other than Ajwa. Ibn Jarir said: It refers to all date palms. He narrated it from Mujahid and it also refers to Al-Buwayrah. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) besieged them, he ordered their date palms to be cut down as a humiliation, terror, and intimidation to their hearts. Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated on the authority of Yazid ibn Ruman, Qatadah, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan that they said: Banu Nadir sent word to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him): You forbid corruption, so why do you order the cutting down of trees? Then God revealed this noble verse: Whatever palm trees you cut down and whatever trees you left, all of it was by His permission, will, decree, and pleasure. In it is a slap to the enemy, a disgrace to them, and a humiliation to their noses. Mujahid said: Some of the Muhajireen forbade others from cutting down palm trees, and they said: They are only spoils of war for the Muslims. So the Qur’an was revealed confirming those who forbade cutting them down and absolving those who cut them down from sin. They only cut them down and left them with His permission. Something similar to this was narrated with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him). Al-Nasa’i said: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad told us, on the authority of Affan, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath, on the authority of Habib ibn Abi ‘Umrah, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ‘Abbas, regarding the verse: Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots was by permission of God, and in order to disgrace the wicked. He said: They were to force them to leave their fortresses and they were ordered to cut down the palm trees, so this caused confusion in their hearts. The Muslims said: We cut down some and left others, so let us ask the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), Do we have a reward for what we cut down? And do we bear a sin for what we left? Then God revealed, Whatever palm trees you cut down, and Al-Hafiz Abu Ya’la said in his Musnad: Sufyan ibn Waki’ told us, Hafs told us, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Musa, on the authority of Jabir, and on the authority of Abu Al-Zubayr, on the authority of Jabir, who said: He gave them permission to cut down palm trees, but then made things difficult for them. So they came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said, O Messenger of God, there is a sin upon us for what we cut down, or a burden upon us for what we left behind. Then God, the Almighty, revealed, Whatever palm trees you cut down or left standing on their roots, it was by God’s permission. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cut down the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir and burned them. The two authors of the Sahih included it in a similar narration from Musa ibn Uqbah, and the wording of al-Bukhari from the path of Abd al-Razzaq, on the authority of Ibn Jurayj, on the authority of Musa ibn Uqbah, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, who said: I fought al-Nadir and Qurayza, so he expelled Banu al-Nadir and left Qurayza alone and was merciful to them until he fought Qurayza, so he killed some of their men and took them captive and divided their women, children and wealth among the Muslims except for some of them who joined the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so he granted them security and they converted to Islam, and he expelled all the Jews of Madinah, Banu Qaynuqa’, who were the people of Abdullah ibn Salam, and the Jews of Banu Haritha and all the Jews of Madinah. They also have it from Qutaybah, on the authority of al-Layth ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burned the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir and cut them down, and they were al-Buwayrah, so God, the Almighty, revealed about it: Whatever you cut down of palm trees or… You left it standing on its foundations, so by God’s permission, and to disgrace the wicked.” Al-Bukhari, may God have mercy on him, narrated on the authority of Juwayriyah bint Asma’, on the authority of Nafi’, on the authority of Ibn Umar, may God be pleased with them both, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, burned the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir, and Hassan bin Thabit, may God be pleased with him, said about it: The fire in Bouira was so widespread that it was easy for the leaders of Bani Luay Abu Sufyan ibn al-Harith replied: May God perpetuate this act and burn its regions with fire. You will know which of us is pure and which of us is pure And thus it was narrated by Al-Bukhari, but Ibn Ishaq did not mention it. Muhammad Ibn Ishaq said, and Ka`b Ibn Malik said, mentioning the expulsion of Banu Nadir and the killing of Ibn Al-Ashraf: I was disgraced by her treachery, joy, just like time, with its changing and revolving ways. This is because they disbelieved in a great Lord whose command is a great command. They were both given understanding and knowledge, and a warner came to them from God. A true warner who delivered clear books and verses that enlighten. They said: You have not brought anything true, and you are worthy of our denial. He said: Yes, I have done what is right, and the experienced and wise will confirm it. Whoever follows him will be guided to all right conduct, and whoever disbelieves in him will be recompensed with disbelief. When they drank treachery and disbelief, they found themselves averse to the truth. I see God the Prophet with an honest opinion and God is the judge who does not act unjustly So he supported him and gave him authority over them, and he was their best supporter. Ka'b was left dead among them, and after his death, the Nadir tribe was humiliated. On the palms of our hands, then we have exposed his masculinity with our hands By the command of Muhammad, he sent Ka'b's brother a secret message to Ka'b at night. What he disliked, he brought it down with cunning, and Mahmoud is a trustworthy and courageous brother. Those are the Banu Nadir in a house of evil. They were destroyed for what they had committed. The next day, they attacked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him, and he was watching them. Ghassan Al-Hama supported him against the enemies and he was their minister. He said peace and they ruled, but they turned away and disobeyed their order, lying and forgery. They tasted the consequences of their deed, and every three of them would receive a camel. They deliberately moved to Qainuqa and Ghodar, from which there were palm trees and houses. He said: Among the poems said about Banu Nadir was the saying of Ibn al-Qayyim al-Absi, and it is said that Qais bin Bahr bin Tarif said it. Ibn Hisham al-Ashja’i said: My family is a sacrifice for a man who will not perish. The Jews were expelled by Al-Hassan Al-Maznam. They take a nap in the embers of the tamarisk tree, and they exchanged the soft wood for the muzzled wood. If my opinion of Muhammad is true, they will see his horses between the two mountains and he will be seen gliding. Amr ibn Bahtha leads the prayer. They are enemies, and no one is as friendly as a criminal. They are heroes, daring in the battlefield, shaking the edges of the straightened rope. And every thin blade is an inherited sword from the time of Ad and Jurhum. Who will convey my message to the Quraysh? Is there anyone more honorable than them? Know that your brother, Muhammad, is born and bred between Al-Hujun and Zamzam. So, obey Him in truth, and your affairs will be settled, and you will rise from this world to the highest level. A prophet whom God has bestowed upon you mercy. Do not ask him about an unseen matter. Indeed, in Badr, by my life, there was a lesson for you, O Quraysh, and a heart that was gathered. The next day he came to Khazraj, intending to come to you, obedient to the Great and Generous One. Together with the Holy Spirit, he defeats his enemy, a true Messenger from the Most Gracious, with a teacher. A Messenger from the Most Gracious reciting His Book. When the truth was illuminated, he did not falter. I see his command increasing in every place in elevation for the command of God Almighty Ibn Ishaq, may God have mercy on him, has included here many poems containing morals, sermons, wisdom, and details of the story. We have left out the rest for the sake of brevity and contentment with what we have mentioned, and praise and thanks be to God. Ibn Ishaq said: The Battle of Banu Nadir took place after the Battle of Uhud and after the Battle of Bir Ma'unah. Al-Bukhari narrated on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of Urwah that he said: The Battle of Banu Nadir took place six months after the Battle of Badr.
59:6: God the Almighty says, explaining what fay' is, what its description is, and what its ruling is. Fay' is any money taken from the infidels without fighting or mobilizing horses or camels, such as the money of Banu Nadir, which the Muslims did not mobilize horses or camels for, meaning they did not fight the enemies with duels or duels. Rather, those people descended upon it out of fear that God had cast into their hearts out of awe of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), so He made it fay' for His Messenger. For this reason, He disposed of it as He wished and returned it to the Muslims for the purposes of righteousness and benefit that God the Almighty mentioned in these verses. God the Almighty said: "And what God has bestowed upon His Messenger from them meaning from Banu Nadir you did not mobilize horses or camels for it meaning camels but God gives power to His messengers over whom He wills, and God is over all things competent" meaning He is competent and cannot be overcome or resisted. Rather, He is the Subduer of all things. Then God the Almighty said: {What God has bestowed upon His Messenger from the people of the towns} meaning that all the lands that are conquered in this way are governed by the same ruling as the wealth of Banu Nadir. For this reason God the Almighty said: {It is for God and for the Messenger and for near relatives and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer} and so on. These are the expenditures and types of wealth from the spoils of war. Imam Ahmad said: Sufyan told us from Amr and Muammar from al-Zuhri from Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan from Umar may God be pleased with him who said: The wealth of Banu Nadir was among what God had bestowed upon His Messenger, and it would be such that if the Muslims were to attack it with horses or camels, it was exclusively for the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), so he would spend from it on his family for a year’s expenses. On another occasion he said: his year’s sustenance, and whatever remained he would spend on mounts and weapons in the cause of God the Almighty. Ahmad narrated it here in an abbreviated form. The group narrated it in their books, except Ibn Majah, from the hadith of Sufyan from Amr ibn Dinar from al-Zuhri with this chain of transmission. We have narrated it in full. Abu Dawud, may God have mercy on him, said: Al-Hasan bin Ali and Muhammad bin Yahya bin Faris told us, with the same meaning. They said: Bishr bin Umar Al-Zahrani told us, Malik bin Anas told me, on the authority of Ibn Shihab, on the authority of Malik bin Aws, who said: Umar bin Al-Khattab, may God be pleased with him, sent for me when the day was high. I went to him and found him sitting on a bed facing the sand. When I entered upon him, he said: O Malik, some of the people of your tribe have been buried, and you have ordered something to be distributed among them. I said: Why don’t you order someone else to do that? He said: Take it. Then Yarfa came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, do you want Uthman bin Affan, Abdur-Rahman bin Awf, Al-Zubayr bin Al-Awwam, and Saad bin Abi Waqqas? He said: Yes. So he gave them permission and they entered. Then Yarfa came to him and said: O Commander of the Faithful, do you want Al-Abbas and Ali? He said: Yes. So he gave them permission and they entered. Al-Abbas said: O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this one - meaning Ali. Some of them said: Yes, O Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and give them peace. Malik ibn Aws said: It seemed to me that they had brought those people forward for that purpose. So Umar, may God be pleased with him, said: Take your time. Then he turned to those people and said: I ask you by God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are not inherited from what we leave behind is charity? They said: Yes. Then he turned to Ali and Al-Abbas and said: I ask you by God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: We are not inherited from what we leave behind is charity? They said: Yes. He said: God singled out His Messenger with something special that He did not single out anyone else with. God the Almighty said: “And whatever God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge against it any cavalry or camels. But God gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills, and God has power over all things.” So God the Almighty gave His Messenger the wealth of Banu Nadir as booty, and by God, He did not keep it for yourself or protect it from you. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would take from it a year’s expenses or his expenses and the expenses of his family for a year, and he would make what remained equal to the rest of the wealth. Then he turned to those people and said: I ask you by God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that? They said: Yes. Then he turned to Ali and Abbas and said: I ask you by God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that? They said: Yes. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) died, Abu Bakr said: I am the successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). You and this man came to Abu Bakr, you asking for your inheritance from your nephew, and this one asking for his wife’s inheritance from her father. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: We do not inherit; what we leave behind is charity. And God knows that he was truthful, righteous, and a follower of the truth, so Abu Bakr took charge of it. When he died, I said: I am the successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the successor of Abu Bakr, so I will take charge of it as God wills me to take charge of it. So you and this man came, both of you together and your affair is one, and you asked me for it. I said: If you wish, I will give it to you on the condition that you pledge to God that you will take charge of it as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took charge of it. So you took it from me on that basis, then you came to me so that I may judge between you in a different way, and by God, I will not judge between you in a different way until the Hour comes. If you are unable to do so, then return it to me. They narrated it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri with it. Imam Ahmad said: Aarem and Affan told us: Muammar told us: I heard my father say: Anas ibn Malik told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man would be given from his wealth date palms or whatever God willed until he conquered Qurayzah and Nadir. He said: Then he kept returning after that. He said: My family ordered me to go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him for what his family had given him or some of it. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given him Umm Ayman or whatever God willed. He said: So I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave them to me. Umm Ayman came and put the cloth around my neck and kept saying: No, by God, besides Whom there is no god, He will not give them to you when He has given them to me, or something like that. The Prophet of God said: For you such and such. He said: And you say: No, by God. He said: And he says: For you such and such. He said: And you say: No, by God. He said: “And he says: For you such and such.” He said: Until he gave her. I thought he said: ten times as much, or he said: close to ten times as much, or something like that. Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim through various chains of narration on the authority of Mu’tamir. And this is it. The categories mentioned in this verse are the categories mentioned in the fifth of the spoils of war. We have already discussed them in Surat Al-Anfal, so there is no need to repeat them here, and praise be to God. God the Almighty said: {So that it will not be a circulating wealth among the rich among you} meaning, We made these expenditures for the spoils of war so that it would not remain a food that the rich would monopolize and dispose of based on mere desires and opinions, and they would not give any of it to the poor. God the Almighty said: {And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from} meaning, whatever he commands you - do, and whatever he forbids you - avoid, because he only commands good and forbids evil. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Saeed told us, from Qatadah, from Al-Hasan Al-Awfi, from Yahya ibn Al-Jazzar, from Masruq, who said: A woman came to Ibn Mas`ud and said: I have heard that you forbid tattooing and extensions. Did you find something in the Book of God the Almighty or from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He said: Yes, something I found in the Book of God and from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: By God, I have leafed through the Mushaf from the covers and did not find what you say in it. He said: So what did you find in it: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from? She said: Yes. He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbidding the woman who extends hair, tattoos, and plucks eyebrows. She said: Perhaps it is with some of your family. He said: Then go in and look. So she went in and looked, then came out. She said: I do not see anything wrong with it. He said to her: Have you not remembered the advice of the righteous servant: And I do not wish to go against you in that which I have forbidden you. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Masoud, who said: May God curse the tattooers and the ones who get tattooed, the ones who pluck their teeth, and the ones who file their teeth for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God, the Almighty and Majestic. He said: report of this reached a woman from Banu Asad in the house called Umm Ya`qub, so she came to him and said: I have heard that you said such and such. He said: Why should I not curse the one whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed and which is in the Book of God, the Most High? She said: I read what is between its two covers and I did not find it. He said: If you have read it, then you have found it. Haven’t you read: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. She said: Yes. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade it. She said: I think your people do it. He said: Go and look. So she went but did not see anything of what she needed. Then she came back and said: I did not see anything. He said: If it were like this, we would not have had intercourse. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri. It has also been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: If I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can, and whatever I forbid you, avoid it. Al-Nasa’i said: Ahmad ibn Sa’id informed us, Yazid informed us, Mansur ibn Hayyan informed us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas, that they both bore witness that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) forbade gourds, wheat, pitted meat, and pitched meat. Then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And the words of God, the Most High: And fear God; indeed, God is severe in penalty. That is, fear Him by obeying His commands and abandoning His prohibitions, for He is severe in punishment for whoever disobeys Him, goes against His command, refuses it, and commits what He has warned against and forbidden.

So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, would take from it a year’s expenses or his expenses and the expenses of his family for a year, and he would make what remained equal to the rest of the wealth. Then he turned to those people and said: I ask you by God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that? They said: Yes. Then he turned to Ali and Abbas and said: I ask you by God, by whose permission the heavens and the earth stand, do you know that? They said: Yes. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) died, Abu Bakr said: I am the successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). You and this man came to Abu Bakr, you asking for your inheritance from your nephew, and this one asking for his wife’s inheritance from her father. Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: We do not inherit; what we leave behind is charity. And God knows that he was truthful, righteous, and a follower of the truth, so Abu Bakr took charge of it. When he died, I said: I am the successor of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the successor of Abu Bakr, so I will take charge of it as God wills me to take charge of it. So you and this man came, both of you together and your affair is one, and you asked me for it. I said: If you wish, I will give it to you on the condition that you pledge to God that you will take charge of it as the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) took charge of it. So you took it from me on that basis, then you came to me so that I may judge between you in a different way, and by God, I will not judge between you in a different way until the Hour comes. If you are unable to do so, then return it to me. They narrated it from the hadith of Al-Zuhri with it. Imam Ahmad said: Aarem and Affan told us: Muammar told us: I heard my father say: Anas ibn Malik told us, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: A man would be given from his wealth date palms or whatever God willed until he conquered Qurayzah and Nadir. He said: Then he kept returning after that. He said: My family ordered me to go to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and ask him for what his family had given him or some of it. The Prophet of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, had given him Umm Ayman or whatever God willed. He said: So I asked the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and he gave them to me. Umm Ayman came and put the cloth around my neck and kept saying: No, by God, besides Whom there is no god, He will not give them to you when He has given them to me, or something like that. The Prophet of God said: For you such and such. He said: And you say: No, by God. He said: And he says: For you such and such. He said: And you say: No, by God. He said: “And he says: For you such and such.” He said: Until he gave her. I thought he said: ten times as much, or he said: close to ten times as much, or something like that. Narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim through various chains of narration on the authority of Mu’tamir. And this is it. The categories mentioned in this verse are the categories mentioned in the fifth of the spoils of war. We have already discussed them in Surat Al-Anfal, so there is no need to repeat them here, and praise be to God. God the Almighty said: {So that it will not be a circulating wealth among the rich among you} meaning, We made these expenditures for the spoils of war so that it would not remain a food that the rich would monopolize and dispose of based on mere desires and opinions, and they would not give any of it to the poor. God the Almighty said: {And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from} meaning, whatever he commands you - do, and whatever he forbids you - avoid, because he only commands good and forbids evil. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Yahya ibn Abi Talib told us, Abdul Wahhab told us, Saeed told us, from Qatadah, from Al-Hasan Al-Awfi, from Yahya ibn Al-Jazzar, from Masruq, who said: A woman came to Ibn Mas`ud and said: I have heard that you forbid tattooing and extensions. Did you find something in the Book of God the Almighty or from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him)? He said: Yes, something I found in the Book of God and from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him). She said: By God, I have leafed through the Mushaf from the covers and did not find what you say in it. He said: So what did you find in it: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from? She said: Yes. He said: I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbidding the woman who extends hair, tattoos, and plucks eyebrows. She said: Perhaps it is with some of your family. He said: Then go in and look. So she went in and looked, then came out. She said: I do not see anything wrong with it. He said to her: Have you not remembered the advice of the righteous servant: And I do not wish to go against you in that which I have forbidden you. Imam Ahmad said: Abdur-Rahman told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Alqamah, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Masoud, who said: May God curse the tattooers and the ones who get tattooed, the ones who pluck their teeth, and the ones who file their teeth for the sake of beauty, changing the creation of God, the Almighty and Majestic. He said: report of this reached a woman from Banu Asad in the house called Umm Ya`qub, so she came to him and said: I have heard that you said such and such. He said: Why should I not curse the one whom the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, cursed and which is in the Book of God, the Most High? She said: I read what is between its two covers and I did not find it. He said: If you have read it, then you have found it. Haven’t you read: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. She said: Yes. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, forbade it. She said: I think your people do it. He said: Go and look. So she went but did not see anything of what she needed. Then she came back and said: I did not see anything. He said: If it were like this, we would not have had intercourse. Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs on the authority of Sufyan al-Thawri. It has also been proven in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurayrah that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: If I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can, and whatever I forbid you, avoid it. Al-Nasa’i said: Ahmad ibn Sa’id informed us, Yazid informed us, Mansur ibn Hayyan informed us, on the authority of Sa’id ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Ibn ‘Amr ibn ‘Abbas, that they both bore witness that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) forbade gourds, wheat, pitted meat, and pitched meat. Then the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited: And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And the words of God, the Most High: And fear God; indeed, God is severe in penalty. That is, fear Him by obeying His commands and abandoning His prohibitions, for He is severe in punishment for whoever disobeys Him, goes against His command, refuses it, and commits what He has warned against and forbidden.

Those are the truthful” meaning those who have been true to their words through their actions, and these are the leaders of the Muhajireen.
