Narrated by Al-Bukhari here as well. God the Almighty said: {They love those who emigrate to them} meaning, out of their nobility and honor, they love the emigrants and support them with their wealth. Imam Ahmad said: Yazid told us, Hamid told us, on the authority of Anas, who said: The emigrants said: O Messenger of God, we have never seen a people like us who emigrated to them in terms of providing support for little or giving more generously for much. They spared us the burden and shared in the pleasures with us, to the point that we feared that they would take all the reward. He said: No, as long as you praised them and supplicated to God for them. I have not seen it from this source in the books. Al-Bukhari said: Abdullah bin Muhammad told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Yahya bin Saeed, who heard Anas bin Malik when he went out with him to Al-Walid. He said: The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) called upon the Ansar to grant them both Bahrain. They said: No, unless a similar amount is granted to our brothers among the Muhajireen. He said: If not, then be patient until you meet me, for indeed, you will be affected. Al-Bukhari is the only one to narrate it from this chain of transmission. Al-Hasan al-Basri said, And they find not in their hearts any need meaning envy for what they have been given. Qatadah said, meaning what their brothers have been given. Ibn Zayd said the same. A man from the Ansar came out, his beard dripping from his ablution, and he had hung his sandals in his left hand. The next day, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the same thing, and the same man came out as the first time. On the third day, the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said the same thing again, and the same man came out in the same state as the first time. When the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) left, Abdullah ibn Amr ibn al-As followed him and said, “By God, I swear that I will not enter upon my father for three days. If you see that you will accommodate me until you leave, I will do so.” He said, Yes. Anas said: Abdullah used to say that he spent those three nights with him and did not see him get up at night for anything, except that when he woke up, he would turn over in his bed, mention God and say Allahu Akbar until he got up for the Fajr prayer. Abdullah said: However, I did not hear him say anything but good things. When the three nights passed and I almost began to despise his deeds, I said: O Abdullah, there was no anger or estrangement between me and my father, but I heard the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say to you three times, A man from the people of Paradise will appear to you now. So you appeared three times, and I wanted to come to you to see what you did so that I could follow his example. I did not see you doing any great deeds, so what brought you to what the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said? He said: It is nothing but what you saw. When I turned away, he called me and said: It is nothing but what you saw, except that I do not find in myself any deceit for any of the Muslims, and I do not envy anyone for any good that God has given him. Abdullah said: This is what you have reached and it is unbearable. Al-Nasa’i narrated it in Al-Yawm wa Al-Laylah on the authority of Suwaid bin Nasr on the authority of Ibn Al-Mubarak on the authority of Muammar, and this is a sound chain of transmission according to the conditions of the two Sahihs, but Aqil and others narrated it on the authority of Al-Zuhri on the authority of a man on the authority of Anas, and God knows best. Abdur Rahman bin Zaid bin Aslam said about the verse: {And they find not in their breasts any need for what they have been given} meaning what was given to the Muhajireen. He said: Some of those who spoke about the Ansar spoke about the wealth of Banu Nadir, so God rebuked them for that, saying: {And what God bestowed on His Messenger from them - you did not urge upon it any cavalry or camels. But God gives authority to His messengers over whom He wills, and God has power over all things.} He said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: {Your brothers have left behind wealth and children and have come out to you.} They said: Our wealth is divided among us. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: {Or something else?} They said: What is that, O Messenger of God? He said: {They are people who do not know how to work, so you should suffice them and share the fruits with them.} They said: Yes, O Messenger of God. And the verse: {And they give preference over themselves, even though they are in privation} means need, that is, they give precedence to the needy over their own needs, and they start with people before themselves when they are in need of that. It has been proven in Sahih that the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: The best charity is the effort of the poor. This status is higher than the status of those whom God Almighty described in His words: and give food, in spite of the love for it and His statement: and give wealth, in spite of the love for it. These people gave charity while loving what they gave, and they might not have any need for it or necessity for it. These people gave preference over themselves, despite their poverty and need for what they spent. From this status, Abu Bakr may God be pleased with him gave all his wealth in charity. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said to him: What have you left for your family? He may God be pleased with him said: I left them God and His Messenger. This is also the case with the water that was offered to Ikrimah and his companions on the day of Yarmouk, as each one of them ordered that it be given to his companion, even though he was wounded and burdened and in dire need of water. Then another returned it to a third, but it did not reach the third until they had all died and none of them had drunk it, may God be pleased with them and satisfy them. Al-Bukhari said: Ya`qub ibn Ibrahim ibn Kathir narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, Fadil ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Abu Hazim al-Ashja`i narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: A man came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and said: O Messenger of God, I am in dire straits. So he sent for his wives but did not find anything with them. The Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Is there no man who will be a guest tonight? May God have mercy on him. A man from the Ansar stood up and said: I will, O Messenger of God. So he went to his family and said to his wife: “This is the guest of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him), do not withhold anything from him.” She said: By God, I have nothing with me except the food of the children. He said: When the boys want supper, put them to sleep, and come and turn off the lamp and we will eat our fill tonight. So I did that, and the man went to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) in the morning and said: God the Almighty was amazed - or laughed - at so-and-so and so-and-so. And God the Almighty revealed: And they give preference over themselves, even though they were in need. And thus it was narrated by Al-Bukhari in another place, and by Muslim, Al-Tirmidhi and Al-Nasa’i through various chains of transmission on the authority of Fudayl ibn Ghazwan. In a narration by Muslim, this Ansari is called Abu Talha, may God be pleased with him. God Almighty says: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. That is, whoever is saved from stinginess will be successful and prosperous. Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra’ told us, on the authority of Ubayd God ibn Muqsim, on the authority of Jabir ibn Abdullah, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of greed, for greed destroyed those who came before you. It led them to shed each other’s blood and make permissible what is forbidden to each other.” Muslim is the only one to transmit it, as he narrated it on the authority of al-Qa’nabi, on the authority of Dawud ibn Qays. Al-A’mash and Shu’bah narrated from Amr ibn Murrah from Abdullah ibn al-Harith from Zuhair ibn al-Aqmar from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of injustice, for injustice is darkness on the Day of Resurrection. Beware of obscenity, for God does not like obscenity or obscenity. Beware of miserliness, for it destroyed those who came before you. It commanded them to be unjust, so they were unjust. It commanded them to commit immorality, so they committed immorality. It commanded them to sever ties of kinship, so they sever ties of kinship.” Ahmad and Abu Dawud narrated it from Shu’bah and al-Nasa’i from al-A’mash, both from Amr ibn Murrah with it. Al-Layth said from Yazid ibn al-Haad from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih from Safwan ibn Abi Yazid from al-Qa’qa’ ibn al-Julah from Abu Hurayrah that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: The dust of fighting in the cause of God and the smoke of Hell will never come together in the belly of a servant, and miserliness and faith will never come together in the heart of a servant. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Abdah ibn Sulayman told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, al-Mas’udi told us from Jami’ ibn Shaddad. On the authority of Al-Aswad bin Hilal, who said: A man came to Abdullah and said: O Abu Abdul-Rahman, I fear that I have perished. Abdullah asked him: What is that? He said: I heard God say: And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - it is those who will be the successful. And I am a stingy man who can hardly give anything away. Abdullah said: That is not the stinginess that God mentioned in the Quran. Rather, the stinginess that God mentioned in the Quran is that you unjustly consume your brother’s wealth. Rather, that is miserliness, and miserliness is an evil thing. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated on the authority of Tariq ibn Abd al-Rahman, on the authority of Saeed ibn Jubayr, on the authority of Abu al-Hayaj al-Asadi, who said: I was circumambulating the Kaaba and I saw a man saying: O God, protect me from the greed of my soul, and he did not say anything more than that. So I said to him, and he said: If I am protected from the greed of my soul, I will not steal, I will not commit adultery, and I will not do any of that. And the man was Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, may God be pleased with him. Narrated by Ibn Jarir. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to me, Sulayman ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Dimashqi narrated to us, Ismail ibn Ayyash narrated to us, Majma’ ibn Jariyah al-Ansari narrated to us, on the authority of his uncle Yazid ibn Jariyah, on the authority of Anas ibn Malik, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: He who pays zakat, entertains guests, and gives in times of calamity is free from greed. And the Almighty said: “And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts any rancor toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.’” These are the third group of those whose poor are entitled to the spoils of war, and they are the Muhajireen, then the Ansar, then those who followed them in goodness, as He said in the verse of Bara’ah: And the first forerunners among the Muhajireen and the Ansar and those who followed them in goodness - God is pleased with them and they are pleased with Him. So those who followed them in goodness are those who follow their good traces and beautiful characteristics, calling for them in secret and in public. For this reason, the Almighty said in this noble verse: And those who came after them say, meaning saying, Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts any rancor meaning hatred and envy “for those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.” And how excellent is what Imam Malik, may God have mercy on him, derived from this noble verse, that the Rafidi who curses the Companions has no share in the spoils of war, because he is not described as such. With what God praised them in their saying: “Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith and put not in our hearts any hatred toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful.” Ibn Abi Hatim said: Musa bin Abdul Rahman Al-Masruqi narrated to us, Muhammad bin Bishr narrated to us, Ismail bin Ibrahim bin Muhajir narrated to us, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: They were commanded to seek forgiveness for themselves, but they reviled them. Then she recited this verse: And those who came after them say, ‘Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith.’ Ismail bin Aliyah said, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Umair, on the authority of Masruq, on the authority of Aisha, that she said: You were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, but you reviled them. I heard your Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) say: This nation will not pass away until its last one curses its first one. Narrated by al-Baghawi. Abu Dawud said: Musaddad told us, Ismail ibn Ibrahim told us, Ayyub told us, on the authority of al-Zuhri, who said: Umar may God be pleased with him said: And whatever God bestowed on His Messenger from them, you did not urge upon it any horses or camels. Al-Zuhri said: Umar may God be pleased with him said: This is specifically for the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and the Arab villages of Fadak, and likewise from what God bestowed on His Messenger from the people of the villages, it is for God, the Messenger, and for near relatives, orphans, the needy, and the wayfarer—and for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth—and for those who had settled in the home and faith before them—and for those who came after them. This verse encompassed all people, and no one among the Muslims remained without having a right to it. Ayyub said—or he said—a share—except for some of your slaves whom you own. This is how Abu Dawud narrated it, but it has an interruption. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Abd al-A’la told us, Abu Thawr told us, on the authority of Muammar, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Ikrimah ibn Khalid, on the authority of Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: “Zakat expenditures are only for the poor and the needy, and those employed to collect it, and those whose hearts are to be reconciled, and to free captives, and those in debt, and for the cause of God, and for the wayfarer. An obligation from God. And God is Knowing and Wise.” Then he said: This is for these people. Then he recited: And know that whatever you obtain of anything - a fifth of it is for God, and for the Messenger and for near relatives. Then he said: This is for them. Then he recited: “Whatever God has bestowed on His Messenger from the people of the towns belongs to God and to the Messenger and to near relatives and orphans and the needy and the traveler, so that it will not be a circulating gift among the rich among you. And whatever the Messenger has given you - take; and what he has forbidden you - refrain from. And fear God; indeed, God is severe in penalty. * For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty from God and approval and supporting God and His Messenger - those are the truthful. * And those who were established in the home and in the faith before them love those who emigrated to them and find not in their breasts any need for what the emigrants were given and give them preference over themselves, even though they were in privation. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul - those are the successful. * And those who came after them.” Then he said: This includes all Muslims, and no one has no right to it. Then he said: If I live, a shepherd will come to him while he is in the garden of Himyar, and his forehead will not sweat over it.

Until I saw two piles of food and clothes, until I saw the face of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, shining as if it were gilded, then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Whoever establishes a good practice in Islam will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it after him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. Nothing of your affairs is hidden from Him, and nothing of your affairs, great or small, is absent. When the pulpit was first installed and the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) came to deliver the sermon, he passed the trunk towards the pulpit. At that moment, the trunk moaned and began to groan like a child who is silenced by what it hears of the remembrance and revelation from it. It has been mentioned that the meaning of this would have been this Qur’an. He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.” God the Almighty informed us that He is the only deity. There is no lord other than Him and no deity of existence other than Him. Everything worshipped besides Him is false. He is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, meaning He knows all beings, those seen by us and those hidden from us. Nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Him, whether great or small, great or small, even the atom in the darkness. God the Almighty said: He is the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful We have already discussed this at the beginning of the commentary, so there is no need to repeat it here. What is meant is that He is the Possessor of vast mercy that encompasses all creatures. He is the Most Gracious and Most Merciful of this world and the Hereafter. God the Almighty said: And My mercy encompasses all things. And He the Almighty said: Your Lord has decreed upon Himself mercy. Then God the Almighty said: He is God, other than whom there is no deity.’ That is, the Owner of all things, He disposes of them without resistance or opposition. And the Almighty’s saying: The Holy Wahb ibn Munabbih said: It means the pure. Mujahid and Qatadah said: It means the blessed. Ibn Jurayj said: The noble angels sanctify Him. “Peace” means from all faults and shortcomings due to His perfection in His essence, attributes and actions. God the Almighty says: {The Believer}. Ad-Dahhak said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: meaning, He feels secure from His creation that He will wrong them. Qatada said: He feels secure in His word that it is true. Ibn Zayd said: He has confirmed the truth of His believing servants in their belief in Him. God the Almighty says: {The Guardian}. Ibn Abbas and others said: meaning, He is the Witness over His creation by their deeds, meaning, He is an Overseer over them, like His statement: {And God is Witness over all things} and His statement: {Then God is Witness over what they do} and His statement: {Then is He One who is Over every soul for what it has earned?}. God the Almighty says: {The Exalted in Might} meaning, He who has made everything mighty, subdued it, and overcomes all things, so no one can attain His rank due to His might, greatness, might, and pride. For this reason God the Almighty said: {The Compeller, the Proud} meaning, to whom compulsion is not befitting except Him, and arrogance is not befitting except to His greatness, as mentioned previously in the Sahih: {Greatness is My garment and pride is My cloak, so whoever disputes with Me over one of them, I will punish him.} Qatada said: The Compeller is the One who compels His creation to do as He wills. Ibn Jarir said: The Compeller is the One who reforms the affairs of His creation and disposes of them in a manner that is good for them. Qatada said: The Arrogant means above all evil. Then God the Almighty said: Glory be to God, above what they associate with Him. And His saying: He is God, the Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner. Creation is estimation, and creation is the individual, which is the implementation and bringing into existence what He has decreed and decided. From this it is said that the executioner measured and then cut, meaning he cut according to what he had estimated according to what he wanted. And the Almighty’s saying: The Creator, the Inventor, the Fashioner means the One who, when He wants something, says to it, Be, and it is in the manner that He wants, and the manner that He chooses, as in His saying: In whatever form He wills He has assembled you. For this reason, He said, the Fashioner, meaning the One who carries out what He wants to create in the manner that He wants. God the Almighty says: To Him belong the best names. We have already discussed this in Surat Al-A’raf. We will mention the hadith narrated in the two Sahihs on the authority of Abu Hurairah on the authority of the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him): “God has ninety-nine names, one hundred minus one. Whoever enumerates them will enter Paradise. He is odd and loves odd numbers.” The narration of At-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah on the authority of Abu Hurairah was also mentioned, and after his statement he added: He is odd and loves odd numbers. The context of Ibn Majah includes additions and subtractions, advancements and delays.
